annotation.title_clean: Navigating Psychological Boundaries: A Boundary-Aware Interaction Policy for Adaptive Service Robots in Exhibitions
annotation.title_en: Navigating Psychological Boundaries: A Boundary-Aware Interaction Policy for Adaptive Service Robots in Exhibitions
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Yoon, H.; Kim, M.-G.; Park, C.; Ahn, H.-N.
annotation.summary_en: Korean HRI preprint that surveyed 164 exhibition visitors. It proposes "psychological boundaries" that regulate how open visitors are to service-robot intervention, and builds a cost-sensitive interaction policy to classify visitors early and choose a service intensity. It argues that robots should hold back interventions to respect visitor autonomy. It is a design study, not a governance study.
key_provisions_or_claims: Visitors' service preferences fall into three dimensions: proactive support, adaptive responsiveness, and minimal service that preserves autonomy.
Hedonic and epistemic visit motivations shape how open visitors' psychological boundaries are to robot intervention.
A decision model that weighs the uneven social costs of misclassifying visitors can classify them early and select a suitable service intensity.
Robotic intelligence includes situational restraint: knowing when not to intervene, to respect visitor autonomy.
Funded by Korea's MOTIE/KEIT programme on behaviour-oriented HRI AI technology.
